### 🟡 Changes recommended A failed GraphQL thread fetch can pass the completeness check with partial data and cause false convergence.
1 open issue - [Abort on non-zero GraphQL fetch exit](https://github.com/sgbett/dotfiles-claude/pull/14#discussion_r4390690635) · New
What changed in this PR Hardens `/copilot-check`’s reviewer identity checks and pins vendored architecture skills to a reviewed fork commit, addressing the trust boundaries in #12. **Changes:** - Matches Copilot by account ID and strengthens thread handling, polling and trusted rubric loading. - Pins the vendored fork and documents how to review and update the pin. - Preserves skill symlinks during installation and verifies the installed script, clone and links before reporting success. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `skills/​copilot-check/​SKILL.md` | Strengthens identity checks and review-loop safeguards. | | `SETUP.md` | Documents pinned installation and the review-and-bump procedure. | | `scripts/​vendor-setup.sh` | Clones at the pin and validates existing clones without changing them. | | `README.md` | Identifies the pinned fork and preserves upstream attribution. | | `docs/​copilot-check-automation-plan.md` | Marks login-based identity guidance as superseded. | | `commands/​dotfiles-setup.md` | Preserves symlinks and verifies vendored setup before reporting success. |
Review effort: Balanced

### 🔵 Needs a closer look The unresolved rubric-loading failure and security-sensitive autonomous workflow warrant fixes and end-to-end human validation. **No open issues** 🎉
1 previously missed issue In code that hasn't changed since last review
Abort when PR base branch lookup fails `skills/​copilot-check/​SKILL.md:60` If `gh pr view` fails, this snippet continues with an empty `ref` because the lookup's exit status is unchecked. A subsequent successful request can then report success without having established the PR's base branch, defeating fail-closed rubric loading. Abort on the failed lookup, or reuse the `baseRefName` already obtained in step 1.
1 resolved since last review - [Abort on non-zero GraphQL fetch exit](https://github.com/sgbett/dotfiles-claude/pull/14#discussion_r4390690635)
Review effort: Balanced

### 🔵 Needs a closer look The security-sensitive automation needs human validation, and a verified clone-publication race remains unresolved. **No open issues** 🎉
1 previously missed issue In code that hasn't changed since last review
Serialize clone publication to prevent nested destinations `scripts/​vendor-setup.sh:47` If two setup runs pass the absence check before either moves its clone, the second `mv` nests its temporary clone inside the first run's destination. Both moves succeed and report success, but the existing clone is modified with an extra untracked repository. Serialise publication with an atomically acquired lock and recheck the destination while holding it, or use an atomic no-replace operation.
Review effort: Balanced

### 🔵 Needs a closer look The security-sensitive automation needs final human validation, and the unresolved review-body handling issue also blocks approval. **No open issues** 🎉
1 previously missed issue In code that hasn't changed since last review
Fetch earlier review bodies to preserve unresolved findings `skills/​copilot-check/​SKILL.md:126` An earlier review can still contain an unaddressed body-only finding when a newer incremental review has no findings. Fetching only `last:1` hides that earlier finding, so Phase 2a can report convergence even though it was never verified, fixed or tracked; unlike inline findings, there is no unresolved thread to recover it. Fetch earlier Copilot review bodies too, and exclude their findings only once an authored disposition has been recorded.
Review effort: Balanced

Copilot's review of 15:42 lists one finding in its body with no thread: **Abort when PR base branch lookup fails** (`skills/copilot-check/SKILL.md:60`).

Fixed in 4bf3c2c — the lookup now stops on a failed `gh pr view` or an empty base, rather than sending an empty `ref`, which reads the default branch's rubric. The skill also reads findings from Copilot's review body from now on: before this, 2a read threads only, so this round would have looked converged.


<!-- copilot-check:answered 5669979203 -->

Copilot's review of 15:49 lists one finding in its body with no thread: **Serialize clone publication to prevent nested destinations** (`scripts/vendor-setup.sh:47`).

Fixed in a688ba4 — confirmed that macOS `mv` onto an existing directory moves into it. Instead of a lock, the run checks after the `mv`: if its clone landed nested inside another run's, it points the existing EXIT trap at that copy, which removes it, and fails with "appeared during the clone; re-run to check it". Tested with a publish injected between the check and the `mv`: exit 1, the other run's clone untouched, nothing left behind.


<!-- copilot-check:answered 5670097868 -->

Copilot's review of 15:57 lists one finding in its body with no thread: **Fetch earlier review bodies to preserve unresolved findings** (`skills/copilot-check/SKILL.md:126`).

Fixed in 56b92d3 — 2a now fetches every Copilot review and the PR's comments. A review is to do until a comment of ours carries its `copilot-check:answered` marker, which each of these answers now ends with. Only our own comments count, and more than 100 reviews or comments stops the run. The two earlier answers on this PR were edited to add their markers. The review of 15:33 has no body-only finding (its one finding was an inline thread, already answered), so it is marked here too.

<!-- copilot-check:answered 5669850547 -->
<!-- copilot-check:answered 5670219264 -->

A GraphQL response can contain `errors` alongside partial `data` while `gh` exits non-zero, but this snippet ignores that exit status if `pageInfo.hasNextPage` is still `false`. The round can then falsely converge on incomplete thread data, and the later guard will not catch it if an older recognised Copilot thread remains. Abort on a non-zero fetch exit, including when Phase 4 reuses this query.
